penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: Job seekers are individual consumers; the model requires large volume to generate meaningful revenue, and consumer churn in job-search is extremely high (people stop paying once they land a job).

rationale: The buyer here is an individual job-seeker — a notoriously low-LTV, high-churn consumer segment that rarely pays for tools beyond a big-name platform like LinkedIn Premium. Willingness to pay for a niche job-search aggregator is weak: most job boards are free, and the market is saturated with well-funded competitors (Indeed, Glassdoor, Otta, Wellfound). Even if buildable as an automated alert/aggregation service, defensibility is near-zero — any determined competitor (or LinkedIn itself) can replicate the feature instantly. The b2c-at-scale penalty pushes this below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. This would be a job-alert aggregation service that scrapes or APIs multiple job boards, filters by user criteria, and emails daily digests. However: the market is saturated with free alternatives, individual consumers churn immediately after landing a job, and any data-sourcing approach risks TOS violations with major job boards. A solo non-technical operator cannot realistically differentiate here at sustainable unit economics.
notes: Fails buyer_clarity (individual consumers, not B2B) and willingness_to_pay (4 < floor of 5). Also requires b2c_at_scale to work. Drop.
